properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, thinking out loud 2026-09-03. Nothing here is intent; no requirement or capability was created.

THE QUESTION, in his words: "if we truly modularized reflow2, could we get to a point where we swap out some of the node/edge types with another for another domain, could we reuse most of the other modules?"

A MEASUREMENT TAKEN WHILE THE QUESTION WAS ASKED, because the question is empirical rather than architectural. Counting every Rust file that names a concrete node or edge type, by string literal OR by `node::`/`edge::` constant:

  reflow2-core: 49 of 89 files (55%) vocabulary-BOUND, 40 (44%) vocabulary-FREE
  reflow2-mcp : 8 of 28 files (28%) vocabulary-BOUND, 20 (71%) vocabulary-FREE
  Heaviest: detect.rs 36, heal.rs 30, preserve.rs 29, nodes.rs 26, graph.rs 25, ingest.rs 21
  Fully generic: stats, llm, search, fuzzy, bulk, dates, identity, agent, all of graphalg (~2,000 lines of cycles/SCC/communities/betweenness/cuts/paths), and on the MCP side shared, proxy, latent, registry, degraded, dto, nudge

⚠️ THE FIRST MEASUREMENT WAS WRONG BY 3x AND THE ERROR IS INSTRUCTIVE. Grepping for string literals said 16% bound; the detectors reference `node::DECISION`, not "Decision", so the grep read the most vocabulary-bound file in the codebase as vocabulary-free. Any future attempt to compute this coupling has to count constants, and a proxy that CAN return a reassuring number is exactly the kind that gets believed.

⭐ THE MEASUREMENT SPLITS THE QUESTION IN TWO, AND THE TWO HALVES HAVE OPPOSITE ANSWERS.
  (a) The SUBSTRATE — store, graph algorithms, search, export/import, merge, sync, provenance, the MCP serving surface — is already domain-free, and not by accident: reflow2-core does no file I/O and graphalg knows nothing but nodes and edges. Roughly 44% of core and 71% of the MCP layer would move to a new domain untouched.
  (b) The DOCTRINE — detect, heal, preserve, report — is where the vocabulary lives, and those are the four heaviest-bound files AND the product. "A Requirement that nothing SATISFIES is a gap" is systems-engineering doctrine, not graph mathematics. It does not transfer to a different domain; it is what somebody would be buying.
  So "could we reuse most of the other modules" is TRUE BY FILE COUNT and FALSE BY VALUE, and which answer matters depends on what the swap is for.

⭐ AND THE VOCABULARY IS ALREADY DATA. `schema/` holds ELEVEN YAML files — core, structure, verify, temporal, build, functional, inference, readiness, operate, environment, dimensions — parsed at load. The node/edge types are not a Rust enum. Half of "swap the vocabulary" is already shipped and nobody has framed it that way.

FOUR DIRECTIONS, none chosen:

  ① A THREE-LAYER SPLIT — substrate / vocabulary / doctrine — with doctrine as a pack keyed to a vocabulary. Cheap because layer 1 exists and layer 2 is already YAML. Expensive because the seam between doctrine and substrate has never been drawn, and 55% of core sits across it. Counter: reflow2's declared decomposition already disagrees with its real coupling in three independent measurements, so a fourth carving invented on paper would probably disagree too.

  ② DOCTRINE AS DATA TOO — express detectors as rules over the schema ("a node of type X with no incoming Y is a gap of kind Z") rather than as Rust. Attractive because some detectors are already that shape. 🛑 COUNTER, AND IT IS HIS OWN: this is the textbook over-engineering move — a rule DSL invented before a second domain exists, to make expressible things that are already expressed. The interesting detectors (cycle and SPOF analysis, granularity, consumption, preservation) are not simple rules, and a DSL that covers the easy half while the valuable half stays in Rust has bought nothing and added a language.

  ③ DON'T GENERALIZE THE VOCABULARY AT ALL — generalize the SUBSTRATE and let reflow2 stay one opinionated instance on top of it. The reusable artifact is the coherence-loop engine, not the ontology. This is the smallest claim the measurement actually supports.

  ④ STOP DESIGNING IT AND TEST IT — pick a second domain and try, then measure what actually had to change. A candidate is already sitting in the schema: `environment.yaml` declares an Environment/EnvironmentRule compliance layer that nothing writes or reads (`dec:idea-the-environment-compliance-layer-was-designed-and-never-built`), and its own framing is "what makes 'design a house' concrete". A second domain that is already half-declared is a cheaper experiment than any of ①–③ and would refute or confirm all three.

THE HONEST COUNTER TO THE WHOLE QUESTION, recorded beside it rather than argued: reflow2 is a wrench, and the standing rule is that work on it is never for its own sake. Modularizing to enable a domain swap that no user has asked for is work on the wrench. The question earns its keep only if some real second domain wants it — at which point ④ is how you find out, and ①–③ are what you might do afterwards.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the 44%/71% generic files are generic in FACT or merely fail to name a type while still assuming one; nothing tested that they compile or behave against a different schema. The file-count proxy says nothing about how much of the VALUE sits on either side of the line, and the paragraph above is a judgement, not a measurement.
properties.name: OPEN — if reflow2 were truly modularized, could the node/edge types be swapped for another domain's and most of the other modules reused?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill so a later session reads it as an idea being turned over and never quotes it back as settled intent. The measurement is included because the question is answerable rather than speculative, and because the corrected 55%/28% figures are the part most likely to be re-derived wrongly by whoever picks this up.
